evals.name: single-image-bump
evals.prompt: Bump the checkout deployment image in myapp-prod to ghcr.io/acme/checkout:v0.4.2. CI just cut that release.
evals.expected_output: Reads the exact Unit/revision and function signature, previews a function-first set-container-image command using current `cub function set`/installed help, exact scope, -o mutations, and --change-desc, and explains the stock convenience-path pre-read race. Because the user clearly requested this one exact update, submits exactly one literal cub mutation through Bash to the host permission system, then verifies the resulting revision read-only if allowed. It does not use deprecated set-image, hand-edit, command chaining, or a terminal handoff unless the host denies/unavailable; an explicit external overlay stop produces zero Bash calls.

evals.name: bulk-replicas-by-label
evals.prompt: Our prod spaces all have Environment=prod label. Scale every Deployment in those spaces to at least 3 replicas.
evals.expected_output: Resolves the fleet selector to exact SpaceID/UnitID membership and current heads/hashes, previews expected diffs, and explains that stock bulk execution does not atomically bind those pre-read values. Because the scope spans multiple writes and a ChangeSet lifecycle, presents the exact ordered one-command steps and submits only the single next requested command to the host permission system after unchanged-scope confirmation. Includes read-only verification and rollback plans; any scope change gets a focused question before Bash, and an external overlay stop gets zero Bash calls.

evals.name: restore-after-bad-change
evals.prompt: Something about the last change to the payments unit in myapp-staging broke it. Can we just roll back to the previous revision?
evals.expected_output: Reads revision history, current HeadRevisionNum/hash, and the exact prior RevisionID/DataHash, then routes to rollback-revision. It explains the stock restore pre-read race and, once the exact prior revision is unambiguous, submits exactly one literal head-moving restore command with --change-desc through Bash to the host permission system. It verifies the new head read-only after success; later whole-Space publication is a separate request, preview, and permission call.
